evidence: Gates: both criteria binary with aggregation all_pass (task/tests/gates/render/judge.toml:15,20; gates/constraints/judge.toml:15,20), matching scoring.toml [gates] render/constraints = 0.0 and the deterministic requirement that gate criteria be binary. Functional: all 41 criteria are type = "binary" (scored/functional/judge.toml lines 26..404) and each is a pass/fail behaviour with an explicit 'Fails if ...' condition (e.g. hro_move_one_stage:56 skip refused / one-stage move accepted; hro_anonymous:191 refused with 401; hro_live_board:290 within 15 s without reload) - none grades a degree of craft. Polish: 5 criteria, all binary (scored/polish/judge.toml:20,29,38,47,56), each a discrete preservation/behaviour outcome (draft text, document.activeElement, scroll not reset, failed send keeps text and sends once, session-resume isolation) - binary fits; this matches the template's polish shape (template polish judge.toml all binary). Visual: 5 craft criteria (hro_vis_type/color/layout/hierarchy/consistency) are type = "likert", points = 5, each with described anchors at every level 5..1 (scored/visual/judge.toml:20-29, 35-44, 50-59, 65-74, 80-89), matching the template's shipped visual format (template visual judge.toml likert points=5). visual/prompt.md:12,16 tie the gate failure and NOT EXERCISED outcomes to raw Likert 1 (normalizes to zero) and tells the judge to 'grade every criterion independently with its five anchors'; functional/polish prompts consistently use binary 0. Per SKILL.md 'Likert versus weighted' false positive and quality-checks.md:170, the presence of likert is not flagged despite the internal annotation; I found no binary craft criterion (no lost gradation) and no likert block missing anchors. score.py is byte-identical to the template, so no task-side change to likert normalization. Counterexample search: (a) broken-but-passing: an ugly but functional app cannot hide behind binary visual rows because visual is graded on 5 anchors; a visually polished dead app is zeroed by the visual prompt gate (prompt.md:11-12) and the functional floor (scoring.toml floors functional=0.05). (b) conforming-but-failing: the only threshold-like binaries (hro_pol_earlier_place 'within a few pixels', 15-second live windows) are measurable behaviour thresholds stated publicly in criteria, not craft judgements, so binary is appropriate; no conforming app loses gradation through type choice. Scope limitation: this is a source/schema review; no configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index.json scope: 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'), so actual judge use of the anchors is unmeasured - that is owned by the runtime/discrimination rows (40/42), not a type-fit defect.
